title: Wumei Wan restores the colonic mucus barrier by modulating TGF-beta/Smad signaling to promote goblet cell differentiation in ulcerative colitis.
authors: Feng, Yaqian; Chen, Yangyang; Pan, Mengting; Li, Chi; Han, Jiarong; Chen, Jiani; Jiang, Yanling; Ge, Lilin; Chen, Yuanping; Xu, Shaohua; Tao, Lei; Wang, Qingshui; Lin, Yao
one_liner_zh: 该文研究中药乌梅丸通过TGF-beta/Smad信号促进杯状细胞分化修复结肠黏液屏障，属于纯湿实验与表型研究，无蛋白质-DNA互作、无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Wumei Wan (WMW), a traditional Chinese medicine formula first documented in Treatise on Febrile Diseases (Eastern Han Dynasty), was originally indicated for chronic diarrhea or dysentery. Contemporary pharmacological studies have further confirmed its definite efficacy against ulcerative colitis (UC); however, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain elusive. AIM OF THE STUDY: Anti-inflammatory strategies fail to disrupt the "injury-immune activation-re-injury" vicious cycle in UC, rendering restoration of the epithelial barrier a promising therapeutic direction. This study centers on the classical formula WMW to systematically elucidate its molecular mechanism in ameliorating UC, with a particular focus on goblet cell fate regulation and mucus barrier restoration. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Using a DSS-colitis model to evaluate WMW efficacy, we integrated quantitative proteomics, single-cell RNA sequencing and colonic organoids to delineate the landscape that drives goblet-cell differentiation, and identified key proteins by Western blot and immunofluorescence. UHPLC-HRMS profiling and molecular docking further provided phytochemical evidence, thereby achieving cross-scale validation from animal phenotype to cell fate. RESULTS: WMW markedly ameliorated DSS-induced colitis and restored the mucus barrier. Proteomics and single-cell RNA-seq revealed that WMW specifically up-regulated goblet-cell core proteins, expanded the pools of mature and progenitor goblet cells, and accelerated epithelial progenitor differentiation toward this lineage. In vitro colonic organoid and cell-line assays coupled with Western blot/immunofluorescence showed that WMW inhibited TGF-beta-Smad2/3 signaling, thereby activating the differentiation program. CONCLUSION: WMW drives intestinal progenitors toward a goblet-cell fate via the TGF/Smad axis, expands the goblet-cell pool and restores the UC mucus barrier, offering a therapeutic strategy distinct from simple anti-inflammation.
abstract_zh: 民族药理学相关性：乌梅丸（WMW），一种首载于《伤寒论》（东汉时期）的传统中药方剂，最初用于治疗慢性腹泻或痢疾。当代药理学研究进一步证实了其对溃疡性结肠炎（UC）的确切疗效；然而，其潜在分子机制仍不明确。研究目的：抗炎策略无法打破UC中“损伤-免疫激活-再损伤”的恶性循环，使得上皮屏障的修复成为有前景的治疗方向。本研究以经典方剂WMW为核心，系统阐明其改善UC的分子机制，特别关注杯状细胞命运调控和黏液屏障修复。材料与方法：利用DSS结肠炎模型评估WMW疗效，我们整合了定量蛋白质组学、单细胞RNA测序和结肠类器官，以描绘驱动杯状细胞分化的全景图，并通过Western blot和免疫荧光鉴定关键蛋白。UHPLC-HRMS分析和分子对接进一步提供了植物化学证据，从而实现了从动物表型到细胞命运的跨尺度验证。结果：WMW显著改善DSS诱导的结肠炎并修复黏液屏障。蛋白质组学和单细胞RNA-seq显示，WMW特异性上调杯状细胞核心蛋白，扩大成熟和祖细胞杯状细胞池，并加速上皮祖细胞向该谱系分化。体外结肠类器官和细胞系实验结合Western blot/免疫荧光表明，WMW抑制TGF-beta-Smad2/3信号通路，从而激活分化程序。结论：WMW通过TGF/Smad轴驱动肠道祖细胞向杯状细胞命运分化，扩大杯状细胞池并恢复UC黏液屏障，提供了一种不同于单纯抗炎的治疗策略。
